hero.headline: Four arrested after armed robbery and pursuit in Martin County
hero.teaser: Four people accused in an armed robbery of a teenager were arrested after a pursuit in Martin County, according to deputies.
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office arrested four suspects Monday following an armed robbery of a teenager and subsequent pursuit. Deputies say the incident involved the robbery of a teen victim.

The suspects were taken into custody after the pursuit concluded in Martin County. The sheriff's office has charged the four individuals in connection with the armed robbery case.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound getting first Aldi grocery store at former Winn-Dixie site on July 9
cards.body:
Hobe Sound is getting its first Aldi store when the new grocery store opens July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road. The location previously housed a Winn-Dixie store.

Aldi has converted multiple Winn-Dixie stores across South Florida over the past few years. A grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony will take place July 9 at 8:30 a.m.

The first 200 customers will receive a gift bag with Aldi products and a gift card. The Hobe Sound Aldi will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.

The new store brings a discount grocery option to the Hobe Sound community, which previously lost the Winn-Dixie that operated at the SE Bridge Road location.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds skips Florida GOP governor debate, dominates discussion anyway as rivals split anti-frontrunner vote
cards.body:
U.S. Representative Byron Donalds, the Trump-backed frontrunner in Florida's Republican gubernatorial race, refused to participate in the state's first major GOP debate Thursday night but became the central focus of the two-hour event. Former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lt. Jay Collins and businessman James Fishback took the stage and mentioned Donalds by name at least 60 times as each tried to position himself as the strongest alternative to the absent candidate.

Moderator Patrick Bet-David opened the debate by calling Donalds "the elephant not in the room" and explained that Donalds declined to attend because he has raised roughly $100 million and polls between 48% and 58%. Bet-David said Donalds told him he would only consider debating once another candidate hits double digits in polling, summarizing Donalds' response as "Till then, I'm not showing up." Collins criticized Donalds for skipping the event, saying "We don't do kings in the United States of America. We sure don't do them in Florida." He added that if Donalds wants the governor's mansion, "you've got to grow a spine, you've got to stand up, and you've got to fight for the people of Florida." Renner called Donalds' absence disrespectful and argued that every voter in Florida deserves a debate. Fishback contrasted Donalds' fundraising advantage with his own campaign's claim to be the first Florida gubernatorial campaign to visit all 67 counties. Donalds told WPLG previously that "If the race was close, and we were battling it out, we would be debating right now."

The debate centered on property taxes, insurance, affordability and hyperscale data centers. Fishback promised to completely abolish property taxes in Florida and take a "chainsaw" to local government spending. Collins said cities and counties have a spending problem and need more accountability. Renner said the current property tax amendment does not go far enough and pitched his "Florida First" plan to eliminate most homestead property taxes while shifting burden to tourists, out-of-state investors and large corporations. The sharpest clash came over data centers, with Fishback promising to "reject and remove every experimental data center" in Florida and Renner saying he would call a special session to stop hyperscale projects. Collins urged local control with state guardrails, prompting Fishback to mock his answer as a "word salad."

The debate gave Renner, Collins and Fishback opportunities to draw contrasts and pressure Donalds over his absence, but the anti-Donalds lane remains split among three candidates. Renner emphasized his record as House Speaker, Collins highlighted his military service and role in the DeSantis administration, and Fishback positioned himself as an outsider. With Donalds maintaining advantages in polling, fundraising and endorsements, the debate appeared less like a campaign-changing event and more like an audition for which candidate deserves a one-on-one contest with the frontrunner.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with global artist programs
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce preserves the Crain Estate while connecting local and international artists through residency programs and public tours of the historic property.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation operates on the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once called the property home. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The foundation has maintained 90% of the estate as it was when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling, masculine bathroom colors, and pre-stained glass. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting items for their Florida estate including a gazebo shipped from India.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven birds that have grown to a flock of over 100. Among them is Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognizable by his limp. The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that attracts artists from around the world. Art director Krystal Masters leads one-on-one classes at the art lab for students of all skill levels. Masters said the majority of her classes are designed for students with zero experience who walk out with a piece of art.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with knee injury
hero.teaser: Tennis star Serena Williams withdrew from her Wimbledon doubles match with sister Venus on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old tennis star was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. Williams announced the withdrawal in an Instagram post, expressing her disappointment at having to pull out of the tournament.

"I'm heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles. Coming back to compete again has been a gift, and the opportunity to play alongside (at)venuswilliams once more meant the world to me. I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn't ready to compete," Serena said in her Instagram post. The post included images of four syringes that Serena said "shows the fluid they drained from my knee after my singles match." An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her.

Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in what was the only first-round doubles match that wasn't scheduled earlier in the week. The match had been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover from her injury. Venus, who is 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday together with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool.

The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon. Despite the setback at Wimbledon, Serena indicated she could play again somewhere else soon. With the U.S. Open approaching, she hinted at a possible return to competition. "All I can say," Serena said, "is stay tuned to a city near you." The withdrawal marks a disappointing end to what had been anticipated as a memorable doubles appearance for the legendary sisters at the prestigious grass court tournament.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November
hero.body:
Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. announced the return of the 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival to Vero Beach this November. The festival has become a signature event for the region.

The event will take place in Vero Beach, bringing together local seafood vendors and entertainment for Indian River County residents and visitors. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. is organizing the festival.

The Treasure Coast Seafood Festival has been held annually, showcasing regional seafood and attracting attendees from across the Treasure Coast. The November event marks the 18th year of the festival in Vero Beach.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. will release additional details about vendor participation, entertainment schedules, and specific dates for the November festival in the coming months.
